text: The Patriots' stunning 29-26 comeback victory over the Bills at Highmark Stadium this past Sunday has the entire organization breathing easier after what looked like a potential 1-3 disaster, with Drake Maye shaking off an early-season slump and leading the game-winning drive despite committing two turnovers but also delivering three touchdown passes to engineer the upset that coach Mike Vrabel characterized as critical for the defending AFC East champions. The film breakdown reveals how New England's offense finally broke out after a rocky start to the year, with Maye's clutch performance against Josh Allen earning particular praise even as the narrative around this team's legitimacy gets sorted from the inevitable overreaction department—the question now becomes whether this is genuine trajectory correction or a mirage. But the good vibes may prove fleeting: the Patriots know they weathered the storm against a red-hot Dalton Kincaid in Week 4, only to face a far more daunting tight end gauntlet in the Raiders' Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer combo looming in Week 5, a 1-2 punch that will test whether New England's defense can sustain the performance that kept them in the game against Buffalo.
